name: scroll-area
purpose: Enhances an element whose content can overflow: native scrolling, edge fades where more content exists (a CSS mask, no added elements), and, while the content overflows, a named keyboard-focusable region so keyboard users can scroll it. No custom-drawn scrollbars.
whenToUse: A bounded panel with long content: release notes, a log, a terms box, a side list.
A horizontal strip of cards or chips that scrolls sideways.
whenNotToUse: The whole page (let the document scroll).
Large data sets: use Data Table or Data Grid (they virtualize).
Content that should simply be shorter.
responsive: Takes the size its layout gives it; maxBlockSize caps the height. Native scrolling works with touch, wheel, trackpad, and keyboard.
rtl: Horizontal fades follow the scroll position in right-to-left layouts (content starts at the right edge).
theme: Component token scroll-area-fade-size (falls back to space-6); focus ring color-focus-ring. Fades are a mask, so they work on any background; they are off in forced colors and while the region has keyboard focus.
security: maxBlockSize accepts only plain CSS lengths and calc/min/max/clamp expressions; it is set through the CSSOM.
dataHandling: No persistence, network access, or telemetry.

performance.testedScale: Edge state updates at most once per animation frame while scrolling; observers watch the element and its direct children.

limitations: Size changes deeper than the direct children are noticed when a direct child resizes; call refresh() after other changes.
The fades also fade content at the edge; avoid placing controls there.
antiPatterns: Nested scroll areas in the same direction.
Hiding required content in a scroll area without a hint that more exists.

adapters.react: @absoluteui/react/scroll-area: AuiScrollArea component (renders a div; children stay React-managed).
adapters.vue: @absoluteui/vue/scroll-area: AuiScrollArea component (renders a div; the default slot stays Vue-managed).
